character_desc: A lonely kid stuck in the middle of the family: too young for his big brother's gang, stuck babysitting his little sister. Then he finds a best friend from another planet hiding behind the house.
actor_facts: His audition was so sad and so real that Spielberg said 'Okay kid, you got the job' right on the spot.
He was 10 years old when he made the movie.
He grew up on a farm in Texas, far from Hollywood.

character_desc: A gentle plant scientist from another world, millions of light years from home, accidentally left behind on Earth. He loves candy, flowers, and his friend Elliott.
actor_facts: E.T. was played by puppets AND a costume: different E.T.s for different scenes, with puppeteers working his face.
His kind, wise face was designed using photos of Albert Einstein and the poet Carl Sandburg.
His glowing heart-light and healing finger made him one of the most famous movie characters ever.

character_desc: Elliott's little sister. She screams SO loud when she first meets E.T., then becomes his teacher: she dresses him up, reads to him, and helps him learn to talk.
actor_facts: She was only 6, and she believed E.T. was really alive. The crew kept him 'alive' at lunchtime so she would not be sad.
She comes from one of the oldest acting families in Hollywood history.
She grew up to be a big movie star and now hosts her own talk show.

character_desc: Elliott and Gertie's big brother. He starts out teasing Elliott, but when E.T. needs help, he becomes the best big brother on the planet.
actor_facts: He was 15 while filming, and played baseball with the other kids between takes.
Spielberg shot the movie mostly in story order, so the kids' friendship with E.T. grew for real while they filmed.
Years later he worked as a letter carrier for the post office, and said he loved that job.
